title: Recognize rational numbers (fractions, decimals, integers, positive and negative) and place them on a number line

lesson.title: Every Rational Number Has a Home on the Number Line

steps.say: You already know negative numbers live to the left of zero on a number line, like a minus seven degrees Celsius morning in Prince George. Today we answer one question: which numbers count as rational, and where exactly does each one sit on the line?

A rational number is any number you can write as one integer over another integer, as long as the bottom is not zero. That covers more than you might think. The integer three is three over one. The decimal negative two point five is negative five over two. Zero point seven five is three quarters. So fractions, decimals that stop or repeat, and integers, positive or negative, are all rational. Look at negative five over two on this line: it sits exactly halfway between negative three and negative two.

visual.caption: Negative two point five is negative five halves, halfway between negative three and negative two

steps.say: Let's place a mixed bunch. Suppose your group chat is tracking who owes what after a pizza night: negative two dollars, negative three quarters of a dollar, positive zero point five dollars, and positive one point two five dollars. Cut each whole unit into quarters. Negative two is two full jumps left of zero. Negative three quarters is three little quarter ticks left of zero. Zero point five is two quarter ticks right of zero. One point two five is five quarter ticks right, one past the one. Reading left to right gives the order from least to greatest: negative two, negative three quarters, one half, then five quarters.

visual.caption: Negative three quarters is three quarter ticks to the left of zero

steps.say: Here is the trap almost everyone falls into once. People see negative seven and negative two and think negative seven is bigger because seven is bigger than two. On the number line, bigger always means further right. Negative seven is further left, so it is smaller. Think temperature: negative seven degrees Celsius is colder than negative two degrees. Moving from negative seven to negative two is a jump to the right, so you are going up.

visual.caption: Jumping from negative seven to negative two moves right, so negative two is greater

steps.say: Second trap. Negative three quarters, negative three over four, and three over negative four look like three different numbers. They are the same number. A negative divided by a positive is negative, and a positive divided by a negative is negative, and the size is three quarters either way. All three land on the exact same tick, three quarters to the left of zero. Only one negative sign matters, and it can sit out front, on top, or on the bottom.

visual.caption: All three forms of negative three quarters land on this one dot

steps.say: So here is the whole idea in one line. If a number can be written as integer over integer, it is rational, and it has one exact spot on the number line. Left is smaller, right is bigger, no matter what the sign looks like.

lesson.answer: Rational means integer over integer. Every one has an exact spot on the number line, and further left is always smaller.

practice.question: Your Vancouver bus pass account shows four changes this week: negative two and a half dollars, one half of a dollar, one over negative two dollars, and positive two dollars. Draw a number line from negative three to three marked in halves, place all four amounts, then list them from least to greatest. Which two are the same distance from zero?
practice.answer: From least to greatest: negative five halves, negative one half, one half, two. One over negative two equals negative one half. Negative one half and positive one half are both exactly one half from zero.
